articles.title: Scientists Build a Fake Spinning Black Hole — and It Actually Works!
articles.summary: A team of physicists built a device that acts like a super-fast spinning black hole, but it doesn’t move at all! They used it to pull energy from waves, just like a real black hole might. This could lead to better wireless tech and help us understand the universe.

articles.title: Why Space Games Can’t Show You How Huge Space Really Is
articles.summary: Space is so big that if you shrunk the sun to a grapefruit, Earth would be a tiny dot 49 feet away. Game makers have to cheat to make space fun — real travel would be boring and empty. They use tricks to balance awe and playability.

articles.title: The Deep Ocean Has a Secret Snack Bar — and It’s Powered by Pressure!
articles.summary: Tiny particles called marine snow sink deep into the ocean, and the huge pressure squeezes out food for microbes. Scientists found that up to half the carbon leaks out, feeding deep-sea life. This changes how we think about ocean carbon storage.
